_comment: DV-200 comes in when DV-100's "Do you want the sheriff or marshal to serve the papers ... for free?" is answered No: someone else serves, and this is their proof. Items 5 to 7 are the server's - when, where, who they are, and their signature - and are courtUse. The filer pre-fills only what identifies the case: the two names (items 1 and 2), the court, and the papers in item 4 the packet knows it is serving. Each carries the name of the answer that already decides it, so DV-200 asks nothing new, like DV-140: the names and the court are DV-100's, the No that brings DV-200 in ticks 4a and 4b (DV-109 with DV-100 and a blank DV-120; DV-110), and DV-100's custody box ticks 4c (DV-105 and DV-140). The No box is an attachmentTarget - a box another form's answer ticks - so it is never asked here.

parts.question: What is the name of the court?

person_asking_protection_name._why: Item 1. DV-100 item 1 asks it under this name.

person_to_restrain_full_name.text: What is the full name of the person you want protection from?
person_to_restrain_full_name._why: Item 2. DV-100 item 2 asks it under this name.

child_custody_and_visitation_order_reque.text: Are you asking for child custody and visitation orders?
child_custody_and_visitation_order_reque._why: Item 4c (DV-105 and DV-140) is ticked exactly when the filer asks for custody orders on DV-100 - the box carries DV-100 choice's name, so the packet never asks this; the wording is for the form compiled on its own.

dv200_served_fl150._why: DV-200 item 4d: FL-150 is served, with a blank FL-150, whenever the packet makes it - exactly when DV-100 asks for child or spousal support. The server ticks a checkbox that receives Yes; two conditions with the same word write it once.

dv200_served_other._why: DV-200 item 4i: RA-010 goes with the papers when the filer will attend by phone or video.

dv200_served_other_description._why: DV-200 item 4i names the other document served.
